q1: SELECT name FROM drinker WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT f.bar FROM frequents AS f, serves AS s WHERE f.drinker = drinker.name AND f.bar = s.bar AND NOT s.beer IN (SELECT beer FROM likes WHERE drinker = drinker.name))

explanation: Q1 requires that all beers served at every bar a drinker frequents are liked by them. Q2 includes any drinker who has at least one beer they like served at a bar they frequent. The difference arises when a drinker frequents multiple bars: one where all beers are liked and another where at least one beer is not liked. Q1 excludes them, but Q2 includes them.
counterexample_dsp: A drinker 'Alice' frequents two bars. Bar1 serves only Beer1 (liked by Alice), Bar2 serves Beer1 (liked) and Beer2 (not liked). Q1 excludes Alice because Bar2 serves an unliked beer. Q2 includes Alice because Bar1 serves a liked beer.
